review_method: side-by-side human visual QA of the deterministic Godot artifact against the lawful Commons reference, constrained by the registered camera/DTM geometry and conservative visible-subject witness

observations.finding: The 31.5 degree capture gives the Atomium substantially more frame presence than the rejected 50 degree capture and satisfies the conservative visible-subject lower-bound test.
observations.reason_not_complete: The witness is not a full source bounding box; exact crop, yaw, pitch and historical lens remain unknown.

observations.finding: The deterministic capture foreground is dominated by broad simplified dark/light ground surfaces, while the lawful reference is visually organized around a fountain/open-space composition with denser real-world context.
observations.next_evidence: Resolve fountain/basin and paved-open-space geometry from authoritative UrbIS/Landscape/orthophoto or another lawful documented source before adding geometry.

observations.finding: Known source-positioned public trees are present, but the capture still reads as sparse/repetitive compared with the dense flanking vegetation visible in the lawful reference.
observations.next_evidence: Use official orthophoto canopy/gap evidence to refine only supported massing; do not fabricate missing trees from the incomplete municipal point inventory.

observations.finding: Atomium metal is recognizably reflective, but ground, contextual buildings and much of the surrounding urban detail remain visibly prototype-level and generic.
observations.next_evidence: Prioritize source-backed paving/ground classes and hero-visible contextual material proportions before decorative clutter.

decision: Keep 31.5 degrees as the current evidence-bounded benchmark candidate. Do not call lens/framing resolved and do not mark the hero view realism-complete. The next visual lot should target authoritative fountain/open-space geometry because it is now the largest immediate source-to-game mismatch.
